{"abstract":"We present an effective method of exact solution of the (1+1)-dimensional Dirac equation with a linear scalar-like potential in the context of the generalized uncertainty principle (GUP). The effectiveness of the method depends on knowledge of the energy spectrum of the harmonic oscillator with GUP. We employ the property of the harmonic oscillator that the kinetic energy part of the Hamiltonian is of equal weight to the potential energy part to obtain the energy levels from the deformation of the Dirac equation with a scalar-like linear potential through the generalized Heisenberg algebra of a GUP. Our result fully coincides with the results found in the literature. This paper thus provides an easier, alternative and effective method of exact solution of the Dirac equation with a linear potential with GUP.","content":"Exact solution of the Dirac equation with a linear potential under the influence of the generalized uncertainty principle\n\nWe present an effective method of exact solution of the (1+1)-dimensional Dirac equation with a linear scalar-like potential in the context of the generalized uncertainty principle (GUP). The effectiveness of the method depends on knowledge of the energy spectrum of the harmonic oscillator with GUP. We employ the property of the harmonic oscillator that the kinetic energy part of the Hamiltonian is of equal weight to the potential energy part to obtain the energy levels from the deformation of the Dirac equation with a scalar-like linear potential through the generalized Heisenberg algebra of a GUP. Our result fully coincides with the results found in the literature. This paper thus provides an easier, alternative and effective method of exact solution of the Dirac equation with a linear potential with GUP.","evaluation_overlay":true,"paper_id":1534594,"title":"Exact solution of the Dirac equation with a linear potential under the influence of the generalized uncertainty principle"}

{"abstract":"We exactly solve the (2+1)-dimensional Dirac equation in a constant magnetic field in the presence of a minimal length. Using a proper ansatz for the wave function, we transform the Dirac Hamiltonian into two 2-dimensional non-relativistic harmonic oscillator and obtain the solutions without directly solving the corresponding differential equations which are presented by Menculini et al. [Phys. Rev. D 87, 065017 (2013)]. We also show that Menculini et al. solution is a subset of the general solution which is related to the even quantum numbers.","content":"On the (2+1)-dimensional Dirac equation in a constant magnetic field with a minimal length uncertainty\n\nWe exactly solve the (2+1)-dimensional Dirac equation in a constant magnetic field in the presence of a minimal length. Using a proper ansatz for the wave function, we transform the Dirac Hamiltonian into two 2-dimensional non-relativistic harmonic oscillator and obtain the solutions without directly solving the corresponding differential equations which are presented by Menculini et al. [Phys. Rev. D 87, 065017 (2013)]. We also show that Menculini et al. solution is a subset of the general solution which is related to the even quantum numbers.","evaluation_overlay":true,"paper_id":1226525,"title":"On the (2+1)-dimensional Dirac equation in a constant magnetic field with a minimal length uncertainty"}

{"abstract":"We will show that the Dirac equation under the assumption of a generalized uncertainty principle corresponds to a Schrodinger-like equation with a new effective potential. Next, as typical examples, the potential well and the step potential are studied in an exact analytical manner. The scattering problems as well as the reflection and transmission parameters are reported.","evaluation_overlay":true,"paper_id":1606518,"title":"Minimal length Dirac equation revisited"}

{"abstract":"A paper must meet four criteria before it is publishable in a scientific journal.  
•The content of the paper must match the scope of the journal
•The quality of the paper (method and execution of the research, as well as the writing) must be sufficiently high
•It must present novel results (with the exception of review papers and the like)
•The results must be significant enough to be worth reading about (and thus worth publishing).

After a quick review of the first three items, I’d like to spend some time talking about the last item, paper significance.","content":"How to Write a Good Scientific Paper: Significance
